_comment: GENERATED by tools/parse-sound.py - do not hand-edit. The sound driver's tables and the music data. Format and evidence: tools/tgl/sound.py.

regions.name: Sound command dispatch
regions.description: 21 entries, each a handler address minus one, indexed by ASL A at $9315 on a stream byte in $80-$94. Bounded by structure: entry 20 ends at $9355 and handler 0, the target of entry 0, begins at $9356. Registered in annotations/dispatch.json, which is what seeds the trace with all 21 arms.

regions.name: Hardware channel masks
regions.description: Two four-byte tables: $9771 holds 01 02 04 08 and $9775 holds FE FD FB F7. $96CF indexes both by $0343,X - the hardware channel a soft channel wants - to test and then claim a bit in the busy mask $0306. Four bytes each because there are four hardware channels; this is the allocator that lets seven soft channels share them.

regions.name: Note period table
regions.description: 108 little-endian 11-bit periods, $07FE down to $0004, read by $9596 as LDA $9840,Y / LDA $9841,Y with Y = (note + transpose) * 2. THE BASE IS $9840, NOT THIS ADDRESS: index 0 would land 26 entries earlier, in bytes that are not periods, so the used part of the table starts here at index $1A. The values are their own argument - a monotonically falling run of legal APU period values, halving about every twelve entries, which is an equal-tempered octave.

regions.name: Note duration table
regions.description: 30 bytes, read by $94E6 as LDA $9941,Y with Y = duration byte - $E0. The first fifteen are 01 02 03 04 06 08 0C 10 18 20 30 40 60 80 C0 - a doubling series with dotted values between - and the rest are triplet and tied lengths. BOUNDED BY THE DATA, not by a guess: walking every track in the ROM and censusing the duration bytes gives exactly $E1-$FE, which is indices 1 to 30, which is exactly this many entries. Index 0 cannot occur because $E0 means 'the literal byte after me'.

regions.name: Pitch envelope pointers
regions.description: Four little-endian pointers, read by $964A as LDA $995F,Y / LDA $9960,Y with Y = ((index * 2) AND $7F) - the mask matters, and missing it makes the pointers come out as RAM addresses. They name $9969, $9972, $9994 and $99A1. The table ends where its own first target begins.

regions.name: Pitch envelope data
regions.description: Four sequences of small signed bytes - 02 01 00 FF FE FF 00 01, and so on - each ending in a byte with bit 7 set ($81 or $82). These are per-frame pitch offsets: vibrato and slide shapes. WHAT THE TERMINATOR'S LOW BITS MEAN is not established; a loop point is the obvious guess and is not checked here.

regions.name: Volume envelope pointers
regions.description: Twelve little-endian pointers, read by $95B2 as LDA $99AB,Y / LDA $99AC,Y with Y = index * 2, so index 1 is the first entry. Bounded at both ends: index 0 is skipped by the BEQ two instructions earlier, and the twelfth entry ends at $99C4 with its own first target starting at $99C5. Censusing every $85 command in the ROM gives instrument numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 9 and 10 - a subset of the twelve.

regions.name: Volume envelope data
regions.description: Twelve sequences of 4-bit volume levels, one per frame, named by the pointer table above. The first begins 0F 0F 0F 0F ... - a flat sustain. Extent runs to the first song header at $9ACD.

regions.name: Song data (2 tracks)
regions.description: Music and sound-effect streams, $9ACD-$9ADE. Contributed by: song 0 channel 6; song 0 header. Every track here was walked byte by byte from its header pointer to an unconditional terminator - $82 or $84, which stop the channel, or $80, an unconditional jump back to a loop point. Tracks are merged into runs because songs SHARE bytes: song 30's three tracks begin exactly at song 1's loop points, so it is the same music without its intro. Generated by tools/parse-sound.py; the format is in tools/tgl/sound.py.

regions.name: Song pointers (72 entries)
regions.description: 72 little-endian pointers, read by $97E4 as LDA $9B04,X / LDA $9B05,X with X = song id * 2, after $97CC - bank 0's entry slot 2 - takes the id in A. BOUNDED BY STRUCTURE: the table ends at $9B93 and the lowest target above it is $9B94, the next byte, so it cannot be one entry longer. Five entries point at a byte of $00, which $97E4 treats not as a song but as code: it pushes the pointer and RTSes to it. The rest are song headers - a record count, then that many [channel][9 field] records, the last two fields being the track's stream pointer.
